data.name: q09ISA3MES001
data.label: What are core functions of a Manufacturing Execution System (MES)?
data.description: Select all that apply. MES focuses on executing and tracking shop-floor operations (dispatch, WIP, genealogy, performance). Forecasting and payroll are typically Level 4 (ERP) responsibilities.

data.name: q09ISA3MES002
data.label: Which data types does MES commonly exchange with Level 4 systems?
data.description: Select all that apply. MES ↔ ERP typically synchronizes production outcomes, material usage, and statuses. Finance and PO approvals remain ERP-centric.

data.name: q09ISA3MES003
data.label: Which KPI is MOST aligned with MES performance tracking?
data.description: OEE is a shop-floor KPI tracking availability, performance, and quality — central to MES dashboards.

data.name: q09ISA3SCADA001
data.label: Primary purpose of SCADA at Level 3?
data.description: SCADA provides visualization, alarms, and supervisory control above PLC/DCS; finance and procurement are Level 4 roles.

data.name: q09ISA3SCADA002
data.label: Which features are typical of SCADA HMIs?

data.value: Manual setpoint entry and mode switching

data.description: Select all that apply. HMIs show process visuals, trends, alarms, and allow supervisory input; recipe management is more typical in batch systems.

data.name: q09ISA3BATCH001
data.label: Batch control systems are BEST described as:

data.value: Systems executing recipes via procedural steps and phases

data.description: Batch systems use recipes and sequences (ISA-88 concepts) to execute repeatable operations.

data.name: q09ISA3BATCH002
data.label: Typical outputs from batch execution include:

data.value: Batch records with parameters and deviations

data.description: Select all that apply. Batch records capture execution details, parameters, deviations, and material balances/yields.

data.name: q09ISA3HIST001
data.label: A data historian at Level 3 primarily:

data.value: Collects, compresses, and time-indexes process data

data.description: Historians store high-frequency time-series data for analysis, trending, and compliance traceability.

data.name: q09ISA3HIST002
data.label: Common historian use cases include:

data.value: Process KPI dashboards (e.g., energy per unit)

data.description: Select all that apply. Historians support analytics and dashboards tied to process signals; finance/marketing uses are not typical.

data.name: q09ISA3LIMS001
data.label: Key functions of a LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System) include:

data.value: Sample management and chain of custody

data.description: Select all that apply. LIMS manages lab samples, methods, results, and compliant records — not sales/marketing functions.

data.name: q09ISA3LIMS002
data.label: Which integration best describes LIMS ↔ MES?

data.value: MES requests quality tests; LIMS returns pass/fail with specifications
LIMS calculates payroll for lab technicians
MES sends batch context and sampling plan; LIMS records results and releases/holds product
LIMS issues purchase orders for reagents autonomously

data.description: Select all that apply. MES orchestrates sampling, LIMS executes tests and returns disposition (release/hold); procurement and payroll are not in scope.

data.name: q09ISA3CMMS001
data.label: CMMS primarily supports which activities?

data.value: Preventive and corrective maintenance work orders

data.description: CMMS handles maintenance planning, scheduling, and history for assets and equipment.

data.name: q09ISA3CMMS002
data.label: Which data flows are typical between CMMS and MES/SCADA?

data.value: Condition-based triggers from SCADA to create work orders
Maintenance completion feedback to MES for equipment availability
SCADA sending HR timesheets to CMMS

data.description: Select all that apply. Condition monitoring → work orders; completion status → MES capacity updates. Finance/HR flows are not typical.

data.name: q09ISA3WMS001
data.label: WMS (Warehouse Management System) at Level 3 focuses on:

data.value: Inventory movements, picking, and location control

data.description: WMS manages bins/locations, receipts, picks, and transfers close to the shop-floor, aligned with MOM time horizons.

data.name: q09ISA3WMS002
data.label: Which are common WMS ↔ MES interactions?

data.value: MES requests material staging; WMS allocates and confirms pick
WMS updates MES with lot/serial and location changes

data.description: Select all that apply. Material staging and confirmation plus lot/serial/location synchronization are common integrations.

data.name: q09ISA3SCHED001
data.label: Detailed scheduling & dispatching at Level 3 focuses on:

data.value: Sequencing work orders by constraints (equipment, materials, changeover)

data.description: Level 3 scheduling optimizes short-term sequences based on real-time constraints; long-range planning is APS/ERP at Level 4.

data.name: q09ISA3SCHED002
data.label: Which inputs are typical for dispatching decisions?

data.value: Equipment status and availability from MES/CMMS

data.description: Select all that apply. Dispatching uses near-real-time constraints from equipment and materials; corporate strategy and FX rates are not dispatch drivers.

data.name: q09ISA3TRACK001
data.label: Product tracking & genealogy ensure:

data.value: Traceability of lots/serials and consumed materials back to sources

data.description: Genealogy maps inputs to outputs per batch/serial for recalls, compliance, and continuous improvement.

data.name: q09ISA3TRACK002
data.label: Which data elements commonly form a genealogy record?
data.description: Select all that apply. Genealogy ties materials, process context (parameters, times), equipment, and personnel to produced units.

data.name: q09ISA3MES004
data.label: Which capabilities distinguish MES from pure SCADA?

data.value: Order lifecycle management and operator instructions

data.description: Select all that apply. MES handles orders, instructions, execution context, and genealogy; SCADA focuses on visualization/control; batch execution is a dedicated batch system capability.

data.name: q09ISA3SCADA003
data.label: Alarm management best practices at Level 3 include:

data.value: Rationalizing alarms and configuring proper priorities
Allowing redundant nuisance alarms to ensure visibility
Disabling alarm logs to reduce storage costs

data.description: Select all that apply. Effective alarm programs minimize nuisance, prioritize action, and maintain audit trails for operations and compliance.

data.name: q09ISA3BATCH003
data.label: ISA-88 concepts commonly used by batch systems:
data.description: Select all that apply. ISA-88 separates processes (procedural) from equipment structures, key for reusable recipes.

data.name: q09ISA3HIST003
data.label: Historian integrations that empower MES analytics include:

data.value: Contextualizing time-series with batch IDs and equipment states
Event frames linking alarms to process KPIs

data.description: Select all that apply. Adding context (batch, equipment, events) turns raw signals into actionable MES intelligence.

data.name: q09ISA3LIMS003
data.label: Data integrity principles for LIMS include:

data.value: Audit trails for changes and approvals

data.description: Select all that apply. LIMS requires traceable, controlled data handling to ensure quality compliance and reproducibility.

data.name: q09ISA3CMMS003
data.label: Which metrics typically drive maintenance strategies at Level 3?
data.description: Maintenance KPIs (MTBF, MTTR, schedule compliance) guide preventive/predictive strategies at Level 3.

data.name: q09ISA3WMS003
data.label: Advanced WMS capabilities often include:
data.description: Select all that apply. Modern WMS optimizes labor and locations while ensuring traceability via RF devices.

data.name: q09ISA3SCHED003
data.label: Dispatch rules commonly used in short-horizon scheduling:
data.description: Select all that apply. EDD and SPT are classic heuristics balancing due dates and throughput for near-term schedules.

data.name: q09ISA3TRACK003
data.label: Which integrations support end-to-end traceability at Level 3?

data.value: MES ↔ social media platform for customer engagement
MES ↔ Historian for process context linkage

data.description: Select all that apply. Traceability spans materials (WMS), quality outcomes (LIMS), and process context (historian) orchestrated by MES.

data.name: q10ISA4ERP001
data.label: Which functions are core to ERP systems at Level 4?
data.description: Select all that apply. ERP handles planning, procurement, finance, and HR—not direct shop-floor control.

data.name: q10ISA4ERP002
data.label: Which data flows are typical between ERP and MES?

data.value: ERP sends production orders and BOMs to MES
MES returns actual production quantities and scrap
ERP sends payroll tax updates to MES
MES sends equipment vibration signals to ERP

data.description: Select all that apply. ERP ↔ MES integration focuses on orders, BOM, and actuals—not payroll or raw sensor data.

data.name: q10ISA4SCM001
data.label: SCM systems primarily manage:
data.description: SCM optimizes sourcing, transportation, and inventory across the supply chain—not shop-floor control.

data.name: q10ISA4SCM002
data.label: Which SCM ↔ MES interactions are common?

data.value: MES provides consumption data for supplier replenishment
SCM sends optimized delivery schedules to MES
MES sends operator training records to SCM
SCM sends marketing campaign data to MES

data.description: Select all that apply. SCM ↔ MES links material flow and delivery timing—not HR or marketing data.

data.name: q10ISA4CRM001
data.label: CRM systems at Level 4 focus on:

data.value: Customer order management and service history

data.description: CRM manages customer relationships, orders, and service—not process control.

data.name: q10ISA4CRM002
data.label: Which CRM ↔ ERP integration points are typical?

data.value: Order entry in CRM triggers ERP production planning
ERP sends shipment status updates to CRM
CRM sends PLC ladder logic to ERP
ERP sends SCADA alarm logs to CRM

data.description: Select all that apply. CRM ↔ ERP ensures order-to-cash visibility—not control logic.

data.name: q10ISA4EAM001
data.label: Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) systems provide:

data.value: Asset lifecycle tracking and capital planning

data.description: EAM focuses on long-term asset health, depreciation, and investment—not control loops.

data.name: q10ISA4EAM002
data.label: Which integration is common between EAM and CMMS?

data.value: CMMS sends maintenance history to EAM for asset valuation
EAM sends capital replacement plans to CMMS
EAM sends SCADA alarm logs to CMMS
CMMS sends payroll data to EAM

data.description: Select all that apply. Integration aligns maintenance history with asset lifecycle planning—not alarms or payroll.

data.name: q10ISA4APS001
data.label: APS systems primarily support:
data.description: APS focuses on optimizing production plans over weeks/months, considering constraints and forecasts.

data.name: q10ISA4APS002
data.label: Which inputs are critical for APS planning?
data.description: Select all that apply. APS uses demand forecasts, capacity, and constraints—not control logic or marketing data.

data.name: q10ISA4FIN001
data.label: Financial systems at Level 4 typically handle:
data.description: Financial systems manage budgets, cost centers, and compliance—not process control.

data.name: q10ISA4FIN002
data.label: Which financial KPIs influence production planning?
data.description: Select all that apply. Financial KPIs like cost per unit and inventory cost drive planning decisions.

data.name: q10ISA4INT001
data.label: MES ↔ ERP integration typically includes:

data.value: ERP sends production orders and BOMs to MES
MES sends actual production quantities and scrap to ERP
MES sends SCADA alarm logs to ERP
ERP sends payroll tax updates to MES

data.description: Select all that apply. Integration focuses on orders, BOM, and actuals—not alarms or payroll.

data.name: q10ISA4INT002
data.label: Quality ↔ Business system integration ensures:

data.value: LIMS sends test results to ERP for product release
ERP updates compliance certificates based on quality data
CRM sends marketing emails to LIMS
LIMS sends SCADA alarm logs to ERP

data.description: Select all that apply. Integration ensures quality disposition and compliance—not marketing or alarms.

data.name: q10ISA4INT003
data.label: Maintenance ↔ Asset Management integration provides:

data.value: CMMS sends maintenance history to EAM for asset valuation
EAM sends capital replacement plans to CMMS
SCADA sends alarm logs to EAM for depreciation
CMMS sends payroll data to EAM

data.description: Select all that apply. Integration aligns maintenance history with asset lifecycle planning—not alarms or payroll.

data.name: q10ISA4INT004
data.label: Which business systems typically consume MES performance data?

data.value: ERP for cost and production reporting

data.description: Select all that apply. MES feeds ERP, APS, and finance—not CRM loyalty programs.
